title: Consistent game assets - how people do it?
author: Old-Wolverine-4134
selftext:
For a while now I use Cursor and Unity and managed to get some really nice playable demos for game ideas I have. I love tile based isometric games that use squares/cubes as basic building blocks. I've tried using 3D - worked great with simple colored cubes/tiles. Also tried 2D - much harder to get the level builder right.

But at the end of the day I aways get to the point where I can't get the assets I want in the correct way/style. For instance I find it very hard to get a 2d isometric tile right (imagine grass top with soil base). Managed to draw a template in photoshop and then generate assets with AI that i try to fit in my iso tile template - tedious task with not so great end result. My 3D attempts resulted in somehow nice looking cube/grid based levels but they are mostly simple colored blocks - creating AI textures, consistent style ones, for my cube, also proved impossible.

Any suggestions for tools or workflows?

comments.author: Efficient-Pop-302
comments.body: I like to mood board ideas and when I'm creating assets in Pixquare or Photoshop I just refer back to it. Human brain is better at seeing patterns and divergent artifacts needing corrected. Especially when they're in absolute control of the output.

comments.author: khuzait_haircut
comments.body:
Isometric I tried a bit and realized its futile. Diffusion doesn't understand continuity the way we would expect. I settled on 2D art though and make heavy use of omni and style references. I create a full asset (entire character) then clip out portrait, and add effects. Showing a screenshot here.

https://preview.redd.it/3fyir2v8eu1h1.png?width=2560&format=png&auto=webp&s=51cde9de5bd26269db9678125cd2883ec45dccc9

Do you have claude code? I have it look at images and generate prompts. It can help get the camera and perspective for backgrounds. See if it can draw out sketches and then create prompts for what you are trying to do.

comments.author: Chaibi_Alaa

I almost tried all 3D AI tools, it always fails on some step, after all that, I started doing low poly with Claude code, Unity MCP and Blender MCP. I generate ref pictures from GPT or Qwen and then give the reference to Claude, create a specific workflow, build elements alone to reuse them (window style, columns, elements ..) and then let it build the whole thing step by step. comments.author: Capital-Meringue-168
comments.body:
For me at least, what's worked for tile and prop consistency is locking a single style reference image and feeding it through IP-Adapter or whatever omni-reference your stack supports before generation. You generate the whole set of tiles or props in the same pass with the same reference plugged in, and the palette and lighting stay aligned across them even when the prompts diverge.

  


The catch is iso perspective still drifts. What's been more reliable for me is generating each tile flat top-down, then letting Unity do the isometric projection at render time. The diffusion model never has to understand iso continuity, it just produces clean square textures.

comments.author: Scubagerber

comments.author: Rsloth
comments.body:
[magicpixel.art](http://magicpixel.art) \> select artboard with your art > create with ai > variant > reskin creative. AI will recreate it in different skins while maintaining consistency, or you can put in custom prompts ie. "make it look destroyed".

\* You can choose random (like the armors I generated below)

\* Quantity mode - better for small assets, like these armor items.

\* Quality mode - better for more detailed / larger pieces.

\* Outputs pixel perfect, background removed.

\* Use square assets for best results (ie. 64x64, 128x128, 256x256, 512x512, etc.)

\* You can even reskin whole tilesets.

https://preview.redd.it/o5qejyfdb02h1.png?width=3080&format=png&auto=webp&s=d7064a159fc139bc61553cb61ac269718e821acc

comments.author: hightopgames
comments.body: OpenAI Image2 is way better at isometric than any other AI I have tried. For me the trick was to create perfect building templates in photoshop and have it modify those, telling it to keep the exact footprint, angle and orthographic perspective. It’s really good at changing existing art that has the correct style and alignment. I still end up making fixes in PS, but it’s usually close enough to just warp slightly.

comments.author: BugaiGames
comments.body:
Personally dodnt work with tilea/isometry so l will share our experience, maybe something will work.
Depends on asset and goal:
*  For items usually just rich prompt fixed style part on same parameters / model / lora. Bonus discovery - changing resolution changes everything, even style and details
* When you need same asset in different situations- inpaint / edit / use original as latent input but not always  scalable
* Same spirit eg location elements - IP adapter is great
* Motion sprites - make video and split to sprites
